questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Covid was very much still a thing when I applied for my exchange stay. Therefor it was off big influence which country I actually though I would be able to go to even though the pandemic was still roaring. Therefor I decided to go to the US. After this I checked which universities had semester structures that matched my schedule. Lastly I looked through these colleges and made my priorities based on the courses being offered.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. Generally I received a lot of emails with information regarding housing, courses and semester start. They also made a 'google webpage' with all information they though would be handy for us exchange students to have. And just in all the exchange office at NCSU was always very quick to answer emails with any kind of questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
We had a few introduction days in the beginning where we got a whole lot of information. Because of covid these days was online, why a bit of the social aspect of this unfortunately got lost. However we where quickly able to redeem this after.  

I also had a meeting with my academic counselor about my courses and choosing of this.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Unfortunately we didn't have a lot of social interaction and introduction, but as said this was not possible because of covid. So hopefully this will not be a dilemma in the future years. Generally the online intro days didn't work that well, but again this was hopefully a one time thing.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
You could both get dorm rooms (which is shared two and two) or you could get apartments (with private rooms). 

They had a 'Global Village' which was a dorm where all international students got matched up with an American student in a room. Furthermore they here had a lot of social activities for the international students.  

I personally choose to live in an apartment as I liked to have my own private room and only share bathroom with one other , furthermore we this way had a common area and kitchen where you could be social with your roommates when you felt like it.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
In the apartments there was kitchen per apartment. The dorm rooms often had a common kitchen in the building.  

There where a ton of different meal plan options depending on how many or few meals a day you wanted.  

I personally choose the 'Flex plan' which was basically an all you can eat meal plan, where you could use all the different dinning halls as well as restaurants located on campus. Here you could get everything from Chick-fil-a (fastfood), to smoothie bowls and salads. So there was a wide variety of different food options. I will say though that all the food was very American.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is definitely the easy option as you will get everything fixed for you through the university, you can get it for only one semester without having to pay for a full year, and you wont have to pay any extra fees or get any unforeseen extra costs.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: When choosing on campus housing be aware of where on campus the dorm you are looking at is located! Campus is big, and you don't want to live on the opposite site of where you have your classes.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The enrolment office at the host university contacted me and I had to make a list off classes I would like. They then tried to enroll me in the courses and contacted me about the courses that was filled up, enrolled me on the waitlist or suggested alternative courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The host university was very helpfull and helped me out with everything. Just contact them and they will help you. Otherwise it was just to browse through the course catalogue and figure out which courses are relevant and sounds interesting.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had one course I couldn't get but the host university found a different pretty similar course I could take instead. Then I had a different course I was waitlisted for, and thus got an alternative course instead off. However I ended out getting into the course I was waitlisted on.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you get waitlisted on some of your courses you want, then write the professor and show up for the first two weeks when there are 'shopping weeks'. If you show up, and show you are engaged in the course there is a much bigger chance that the professor will let you into the class. 

Also be aware that they have a ton of sports and creative courses, even though you can't get ETCS points for these, look into them and register for them at the same time as the rest of your classes, as most of these are very popular and will fill up quickly and before you come to campus. So if you want one of these as an spare time activity, then sign up for them!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: There wasn't a lot of courses relevant for my studies on a masters level, therefor I also had some phd courses. The level of the courses are very different from back home, in some ways it is easier, but because the whole structure and learning manner is so very different from pharmaschool it at some times seems harder.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are a lot more exams (most courses had 3 exams in total), and it is much more classroom style teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CBS660 Comparative Molecular medicine 

GN541 Human and Biomedical Genetics 

MB718 Introductory Virology 

GN521 Molecular Genetics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All of them where very relevant and useful. 

Especially the GN541 with professor Cowley was an exceptional good course. This is one of the best course I have had during my 5 years at university. So if you are at all interested in genetics then do you self the favor of taking this course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Non really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Transportation and books. I had expected to use more money of this, but non of my courses required any books, and due to covid was all buses in the area free. (normally they are very cheap as well though)  
However phone plans are really expensive! The cheapest we could find was Mint Mobile, so check this out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is litteraly something for everybody at campus. Both creative things, sports, weekly cinema nights and much more.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Basicly everything. Fotball, soccer, cheerleading, rowing, trivia nights, pottery, rock climbing. Basicly anything you could think off. Most things where both on a varsity level and a club level, so everyone had the oportunity to find the right level for them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just joine a club! It is a great way to meet the american students and not only hang around the other international students. I personally joined the rowing club which I absolutly loved! It is a great way to get to know new people, and at the same time also move your body. I loved the late afternoons on the lake, which also was a great way to get a bit away from campus and see a bit more of the nature. It was a great group of people and I ended out using most of my time hanging out with them, going on trips, parties, game night etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go and drive/hike through the blue ridge mountains. One of the best trips we had! And also go to the beach!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. The US isn't that different from DK.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Again, joine a club of some sorts.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of the people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go out and meet people. Go to all the different activities, and events. Just enjoy and get as much out of it as you can.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: n/a

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people, traveling and exploring

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exams are very different from back home, so it took a bit of getting used to.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
